questions.question: Who asked James Rennel to prepare the map of Hindustan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Robert Clive** was a British officer and privateer who established the military and political supremacy of the East India Company in Bengal.
 
• He is credited with helping to establish British control over India, which lasted until Indian independence in 1947.
 
• James Rennel, a geographer and historian, was asked by Robert Clive to prepare a map of Hindustan.
 
• Rennel's map was one of the earliest detailed maps of India, and it played a significant role in the British administration and strategic planning in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Rennel**

 
 
• James Rennel (1742-1830) was an English geographer, historian, and pioneer of oceanography.
 
• He is often referred to as the Father of Indian Geography for his extensive surveys and maps of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His work provided critical geographical information that was used for military and administrative purposes by the British Empire.
 
• Rennel's most notable work, "A Bengal Atlas," was published in 1779 and included detailed maps of Bengal and parts of Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Robert Clive**
 
 
• Robert Clive (1725-1774) was a British military officer and a key figure in establishing British control in India.
 
• He played a crucial role in the Battle of Plassey (1757), which marked the beginning of British rule in India.
 
• Clive served as the Governor of Bengal and implemented significant administrative reforms to strengthen British power.
 
• Despite his achievements, Clive's career was marred by controversies, including allegations of corruption and his role in the exploitation of Indian resources.
 
 
 
• **East India Company**
 
 
• The East India Company was an English company formed for the exploitation of trade with East and Southeast Asia and India, incorporated by royal charter in 1600.
 
• The company eventually came to rule large areas of India, exercising military power and assuming administrative functions.
 
• It played a key role in the British colonization of India and its economy was heavily reliant on the trade of cotton, silk, indigo, salt, tea, and opium.
 
• The company's rule in India ended after the Indian Rebellion of 1857, leading to the establishment of direct British rule, known as the British Raj.

questions.question: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?

__
 
• The Battle of Plassey was fought on **23 June 1757**, in the eastern part of India.
 
• This battle marked the **beginning of British colonial rule in India**.
 
• It was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj ud-Daulah.
 
• The British victory in this battle was **largely due to the betrayal of Nawab's commander, Mir Jafar**, who sided with the British.

• **Battle of Wandiwash**
 
 
• The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on 22 January 1760 between the British and the French.
 
• The British, under Sir Eyre Coote, decisively defeated the French forces.
 
• This battle marked the end of French colonial ambitions in India.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Buxar**

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement came into operation in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1793**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement was introduced by the East India Company during the tenure of Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• It was an agreement between the East India Company and Bengali landlords to fix revenues to be raised from land.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• Under this system, the Zamindars were recognized as the owners of the land and were responsible for collecting and paying the fixed revenue to the Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Settlement**

 
 
• The Permanent Settlement was also known as the Zamindari System.
 
• The Zamindars were required to pay a fixed amount of revenue to the East India Company, irrespective of the agricultural yield.
 
• This system aimed to ensure a stable revenue for the Company and incentivize Zamindars to improve agricultural practices.
 
• However, it led to the exploitation of peasants and did not significantly improve agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Lord Cornwallis**
 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793.
 
• He introduced several reforms in the administration, judiciary, and revenue systems of India.
 
• The Cornwallis Code, introduced in 1793, aimed to overhaul the administrative structure in British India.
 
• He is credited with laying the foundation of a structured administration in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Permanent Settlement**
 
 
• The system led to the emergence of a new class of landlords who were loyal to the British.
 
• It created a stark divide between the Zamindars and the peasants, leading to widespread poverty and indebtedness among the latter.
 
• The rigidity of the revenue demand often led to the transfer of land ownership and distress sales.
 
• The system was criticized for its failure to promote agricultural development and for exacerbating social inequalities.

questions.question: The Ryotwari Settlement, in which cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, was primarily introduced in which of the following provinces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madras and Bombay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ryotwari Settlement **was introduced in **Madras and Bombay** provinces during the British rule in India.
 
• Under this system, cultivators or farmers had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, unlike the **Zamindari system** where they paid taxes to intermediaries or landlords.
 
• The Ryotwari system was considered more beneficial for **small and marginal farmers** as they had direct access to the government and could negotiate the amount of taxes based on their **produce and income**.
 
• The system also helped in **increasing agricultural productivity** and **revenue** for the government.
 
• However, the system was criticized for being exploitative towards farmers in some cases, especially during **famines and crop failures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Central province **was mainly governed under the** Zamindari system**, where intermediaries collected taxes from farmers and paid a** fixed amount** to the government.
 
• **Assam and Bengal **provinces had a mix of** Zamindari and Mahalwari systems, **where taxes were collected either by intermediaries or directly from farmers through **village-level committees.**
 
• **Punjab **province had a predominantly **Mahalwari system**, where large landlords or Zamindars **collected taxes from farmers** and paid a fixed amount to the government.

questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act enacted in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Vernacular Press Act** was enacted in British India in the year** 1878.**
 
• This law was enforced by the British **to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press.**
 
• The Act was used to **prevent the expression of criticism **toward British policies, notably, the opposition that had grown with the outset of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878-80)
 
• It was enacted when** Lord Lytton **was Viceroy of India; he was known for his **controversial and suppressive policies** during his tenure.
 
• The act stated that any press printing in Vernacular language had to declare all its printing machinery and submit all material for scrutiny before publication. If the content was inflammable or criticised British authorities, it would result in the confiscation of the press.
 
• It was the **first legislation to curtail press freedom in India,** and the press became a medium of both control and revolt during British rule.
 
• The act** provoked widespread criticism and protest by Indians.** It eventually became one of the contributing factors to the nationalistic movements that emerged at the **end of the 19th century.**
 
• The Act was, however**, repealed in 1882 by Lytton's successor, Lord Ripon,** in a move to foster press freedom in India.

questions.question: Which Act was passed by the British Parliament in the year 1773 AD to regulate the activities of the East India Company?
questions.solution:

• The Act provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta (now Kolkata) to administer justice.

• It established a dual system of control by setting up a Board of Control to oversee the political affairs while the Court of Directors retained control over commercial affairs.
 
• This Act allowed the British government to have greater control over the administration of India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Slavery Act**
 
 
• Passed in 1843, this Act aimed to abolish slavery in British India.
 
• It made the sale, purchase, or transfer of slaves illegal and provided for the protection of the rights of those who had been enslaved.

• The Mahalwari system was a land revenue system implemented in British India.
 
• Under this system, the village headman, known as the 'lambardar,' was responsible for collecting revenue from the villagers.
 
• The revenue collected by the lambardar was then paid to the British East India Company.
 
• This system was introduced by Holt Mackenzie in 1822 and later modified by Lord William Bentinck in 1833.
 
• The Mahalwari system was primarily implemented in the North-Western Provinces, parts of Central India, and Punjab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System**

 
 
• Also known as the Permanent Settlement System, it was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• Under this system, zamindars were recognized as the landowners and were responsible for collecting and paying revenue to the Company.
 
• The zamindars were granted hereditary rights over the land and were supposed to pay a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System**
 
 
• This system was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• Under the Ryotwari system, the individual cultivator or ryot was recognized as the landowner.
 
• The ryots were directly responsible for paying the land revenue to the British government.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Madras, Bombay, parts of Assam, and Coorg provinces.
 
 
 
• **Iqtadari System**
 
 
• The Iqtadari system was introduced during the Delhi Sultanate period.
 
• Under this system, the land was divided into Iqtas, and the responsibility of collecting revenue was given to the Iqtadars.
 
• The Iqtadars were responsible for maintaining law and order and providing military assistance to the Sultan.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Regulating Act, 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Regulating Act, 1773 was the first act passed by the British Parliament to control the administration of the East India Company in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary oversight and introduced significant administrative reforms in the governance of the company.
 
• The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings being the first to hold this position.
 
• The Governor-General was given authority over the presidencies of Madras and Bombay, establishing a centralized administrative structure.
 
• A Supreme Court was also established in Calcutta (now Kolkata) as part of the act to administer justice according to British law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Government of India Act, 1858**

 
 
• This act marked the end of the East India Company's rule and the beginning of direct control by the British Crown.
 
• It transferred the administration of India to the British monarchy, establishing the office of the Secretary of State for India.
 
• The act aimed to improve governance and centralize authority under the British government.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1909**
 
 
• Also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, this act introduced significant changes in the Indian legislative structure.
 
• It expanded the legislative councils at both central and provincial levels and allowed for greater Indian representation.
 
• The act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a significant development in Indian political history.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• This was the longest act passed by the British Parliament concerning the governance of India.
 
• It proposed the establishment of a federal structure in India, including the creation of provinces and princely states.
 
• The act introduced provincial autonomy and expanded the electorate significantly.
 
• It laid the foundation for the eventual independence and partition of India in 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first state to be annexed into the British empire under the Doctrine of Lapse introduced by Lord Dalhousie?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The first state to be annexed into the British empire under the Doctrine of Lapse was **Satara**, in the year **1848**.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by **Lord Dalhousie.**
 
• The **Doctrine of lapse** stated that: 
 
 
• The ruler of any princely state which governed directly or indirectly by the British does not have a legal male heir then his state will be annexed by the British.
 
• Adopted sons are not accepted as legal heirs of the policy.
 
 
 
• The scheme was the British annexation policy without a direct, natural, or adopted heir which was how the British acquire the many Indian States.
 
• The states that were annexed, followed by Satara were Jaitpur and Sambalpur(1849), Bhagat(1850), Udaipur(1852), Jhansi(1853), and Nagpur(1854).

questions.question: Which of the following Acts abolished the East India Company's monopoly of trade with China?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1833**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** abolished the East India Company's monopoly of trade with China.
 
• This act was one of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company.
 
• The act marked the beginning of the end of the commercial activities of the company, focusing more on administration.
 
• It also allowed the company to continue its territorial possessions in India but under strict regulation by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** is also notable for making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, consolidating the administration.
 
• The act also introduced a system of open competition for the selection of civil servants, although it was not implemented until the 1850s.
 
• It is considered a significant step towards the centralization of the administration in India.
 
• Other important provisions included the establishment of a law commission and the codification of laws.

questions.question: Battle of Buxar was fought in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1764__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought between the English Forces (Hector Munro – British Army Major), and a joint army of the Nawab of Oudh, Nawab of Bengal, and the Mughal Emperor.
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764. Hence the correct answer is 1764. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The reasons for battle were:

 
• Mir Qasim wanted to be independent and shifted his capital to Munger Fort from Calcutta. 
 
• These factors fuelled the English to overthrow him and war broke out between Mir Kasim and the Company in 1763.
 
• Participants of the Battle of Buxar were:
 
 
• Mir Qasim – (Administering Bengal in place of Mir Jafar – Nawab of Bengal)
 
• Shuja-Ud-Daulah – Nawab of Awadh (Oudh)
 
• Shah Alam II – Mughal Emperor
 
 

Result of Battle of Buxar:

 
• Mir Jafar (Nawab of Bengal) handed over districts of Midnapore, Burdwan, and Chittagong to the English for the maintenance of their army.
 
• The English were also permitted duty-free trade in Bengal, except for a duty of two per cent on salt.
 
• Clive made political settlements with Emperor Shah Alam II and Shuja-Ud-Daula of Awadh in the Treaty of Allahabad.
